legend: The self-maintaining haematopoietic stem cells in the bone marrow give rise to common monocyte progenitors and common dendritic cell (DC) precursors. The latter differentiate into either conventional (cDC) or plasmacytoid (pDC) dendritic cells. Monocytes can further differentiate into monocyte-derived cells, macrophages, and DCs under certain conditions. Macrophages originally present in tissues have an embryonic origin and maintain themselves. TH, T helper; IFN, interferon.
